link_slow.title: Powerline: link slower than usual
link_slow.message: The connection **{source} ↔ {destination}** has been much slower than usual for {minutes} minutes: {average} Mbit/s (typical: ~{baseline} Mbit/s).

adapter_removed.title: Powerline: adapter removed
adapter_removed.message: Adapter **{name}** ({mac}) has disappeared from the powerline network and was removed from the topology.

adapter_new.title: Powerline: new adapter
adapter_new.message: New adapter **{name}** ({mac}) joined the powerline network.

recurring_load.title: Powerline: recurring interference suspected
recurring_load.message: The link **{source} ↔ {destination}** has repeatedly dipped at similar times of day. A household appliance or switched-mode power supply (for example a washing machine, refrigerator, or charger) may be causing interference. Check whether the pattern follows a device switching on; test nearby devices one at a time. This is a likely cause, not a confirmed diagnosis.

isolated_weak_link.title: Powerline: one link is persistently weaker
isolated_weak_link.message: The link **{source} ↔ {destination}** remains much slower than other links (current ~{average} Mbit/s; other links typically ~{peer_average} Mbit/s). A power strip or surge protector may attenuate the signal. Try plugging both adapters directly into wall outlets, bypassing extension leads and surge-protected strips.

directional_asymmetry.title: Powerline: TX/RX rates are asymmetric
directional_asymmetry.message: The link **{source} ↔ {destination}** reports TX {tx} and RX {rx} Mbit/s. A noise source near one endpoint may be responsible. Inspect chargers, LED drivers, power supplies, and appliances near both adapters; disconnect candidates one at a time to test. The readings suggest a possibility, not certainty.
